Issued to:
Damietta Combined Cycle Power Station

Procedure:
Weekly inspection of automatic operation (I2-W1)

This document explains the steps of the weekly inspection of the automatic operation of the fire water pumps. The fire water pumps consist of the jockey pump and two other pumps, one the main pump, which is the electric pump, and the second the standby pump, which is driven by a diesel engine. The jockey pump maintains a constant pressure in the fire water lines within the required operating limits: it operates automatically to compensate for leaks in the fire water lines and then stops automatically when the normal pressure is restored. If there is a large increase in fire water consumption, which happens when one of the fire systems operates, or the fire hydrants are opened, or the solar tank cooling water monitors are opened, the jockey pump cannot compensate for the drop in pressure, which leads to the electric pump starting automatically. If the electric pump cannot restore the pressure within a set time, as a result of a rise in fire water consumption exceeding its capacity, or if the electrical supply to it is interrupted, this leads to the fire diesel starting automatically in parallel with the electric pump, and in this case both the electric and diesel pumps continue to operate until they are stopped manually. This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed - Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department - and approved by Eng. Ahmed El-Husseiny Abdullah, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan - Head of the Damietta Power Generation Station Sector - and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of the Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector at the East Delta Electricity Production Company.
No special tools are needed during the inspection rounds
Slowly open one of the fire water line drain valves
Observe the drop in the fire water network pressure
Record the pressure reading at which the jockey pump starts automatically
Close the drain valve opened in step (1)
Observe the rise in the fire water network pressure resulting from the jockey pump operation
Record the pressure reading at which the jockey pump stops automatically
Quickly open one of the fire water line drain valves
Observe the drop in the fire water network pressure
Note that the jockey pump in this case is unable to compensate for the rapid drop in the fire water network pressure
Record the pressure reading at which the electric jockey pump starts automatically
Observe the rise in the fire water network pressure resulting from the electric pump operation
Note that the electric pump does not stop automatically when the fire water network pressure returns to its normal condition
Record the pressure reading at which the jockey pump stops automatically
